description: >
  Pi embeds the portable

lines.text: **Status:** design charter only (2026-10-18), no code or backend switch. **Owner:** FiberOpticsSDK. **Authority:** existing Rust-runtime normative requirements/ADRs outrank this additive charter; cross-program decisions: https://github.com/jehalladay/FiberOpticsResearch/tree/main/docs/research/foa/programs/universal-reactive-rendering-2026-10-18.

The historical Rust migration revision was inspected at a516eba8ba1e4f71382a33f1dadc25322a0e4bee; the connected repository did not expose a live ref called rust-runtime on 2026-10-18. It showed portable workspace members fiber-model/fiber-core/fiber-runtime, native-only fiber-python and replay observers, tests/audits protecting no-ambient-API and no-third-party dependencies, and an incomplete PyO3 graph surface. Before implementation, locate/reconcile actual Rust branch/history, fresh heads and main, and rerun existing gates. This charter neither copies code from that revision nor declares it current.

Retain Cargo wasm_subset classification and policy audit in existing normative files. Portable core owns graph validation, refs, dependency capture, scheduling, propagation, transaction/event records, bridge admission, snapshot semantics and replay after implementation. Host capabilities supply clocks/timers/randomness/spawn; the core never imports DOM, JS or networking. Implement browser-capable artifact/bindings outside portable crates (new nonportable adapter target is allowed with documented manifest classification). Preserve canonical value semantic equality versus content-version relation and their independent oracles.

- Versioned WASM ABI: initialize(snapshot, capabilities), applyBatch(typedCommands, expectedEpoch), inspect(publicRefs), subscribe(viewSpec), snapshot() and close(); browser-side opaque handles are runtime-scoped.
- HostCapabilitySet supplies Clock, Timer, Randomness, Spawner explicitly; real and deterministic fake implementations.
- ChangedViewReceipt carries source runtime/epoch, transaction ref, changed materializations, diagnostics, dependency frontier and trace ref. The portable core does not construct DOM patches.

blocks.text: The Workbench imports the local npm artifacts below. Their exact bytes are part of the package lockfile and execution deployment basis. These artifacts contain SDK clients, not the native Forge, Furnace, or HyperUnix executables. Install those executables independently. Do not infer runtime compatibility from the shared SDK version alone.
blocks.markdown: The Workbench imports the local npm artifacts below. Their exact bytes are part of the package lockfile and execution deployment basis. These artifacts contain SDK clients, not the native Forge, Furnace, or HyperUnix executables. Install those executables independently. Do not infer runtime compatibility from the shared SDK version alone.

blocks.text: Artifacts were packaged from the corresponding in-house TypeScript SDK distributions during development on 2026-10-15. furnace-sdk-0.1.0.tgz was re-packaged on 2026-10-17 (wb-zby) from Furnace revision 9970621d8 (sdk/typescript: npm run build && npm pack, 0 tsc diagnostics), whose contract manifest smithy_model_digest and generated provenance digest agree (sha256:2cf7c539f9f3...); the 2026-10-15 artifact carried a manifest digest (b044cbe9...) beside validators generated from another model (e5995480...), so its loadContract() refused every context decode and the Furnace-hosted adapter failed closed on it. The checksums identify what this consumer installs. They do not establish that the producing checkouts were clean or that every native runtime supports every SDK method. The adapters use independently exercised methods and preserve native errors, coverage, and evidence.

blocks.text: ReactiveFiberCLI currently uses its installed CLI JSON envelope. No unverified TypeScript client or invented SDK method is substituted. Its preview is explicitly noncommitted and carries no durable render identifier.

The initialized RF fixture tier is WORKBENCH_RF_FIXTURE=/absolute/test/workspace forge run rf-preview. Neither tier initializes a native store in this package merely to obtain an empty result.

blocks.text: The native SDK dependencies are explicitly bundled in the npm artifact. A file:vendor/... declaration alone is insufficient for installing a packed parent: npm resolves those dependencies before the parent extraction makes its vendor directory available. forge run install-smoke creates a separate consumer and proves the packed SDK dependencies can actually be imported. It does not prove each native executable is installed in that consumer.

blocks.text: dependency-lock.json preserves the exact npm lockfile inside the distributed artifact because npm excludes the root package-lock.json when packing. The package smoke requires byte-identical lock copies. Installed invocation identity validates the shipped lock against the package manifest and vendor artifact integrities.
